cards.text: This is a song by David, the servant of the LORD. He sang it on the day the LORD delivered him from all his enemies and from Saul, the king who searched for him day after day (1 Samuel 23:14). And when you've been chased THAT long, friend, you don't write a little jingle. You write FIFTY verses.

cards.question: Before David tells any of the story, how does he open the song?

answers.text: He tells the LORD he loves Him
He asks the LORD why He waited
He lists his enemies by name

cards.text: Then David starts stacking up names for the LORD like cookie boxes: my rock, my fortress, my deliverer, my shield, my stronghold. And he's STILL going, friend. I can't get two words out before my first batch.

cards.question: Rock, fortress, shield, stronghold. Every one of those names David gives the LORD is something that ___ him.
True or false: David says that calling on the LORD is how he'll be saved from his enemies.

cards.text: Then David remembers how close it got: the cords of death and of Sheol wrapped him up, and the torrents of chaos overwhelmed him. I got tangled in some rubber bands in a junk drawer once and called it a crisis, so I'm gonna sit DOWN for this one.

cards.question: Wrapped up by death and overwhelmed by chaos, what does David do in his distress?

answers.text: He calls on the LORD for help
He tries to break free alone
He gives up and stays silent

cards.question: David cries out to his God for help. From where does the LORD hear his voice?

cards.text: Then the earth shakes and quakes, and the foundations of the mountains tremble. Okay. Okay, friend, something BIG is happening.

cards.question: The earth and the mountains shake because the LORD burned with ___.

cards.text: Smoke rises from His nostrils and fire from His mouth, and He parts the heavens and comes down with dark clouds beneath His feet. I get excited when my oven PREHEATS, and the LORD just parted the HEAVENS.

cards.question: The LORD is coming down from the heavens. What does He mount and fly on?

cards.text: He makes darkness His hiding place, with storm clouds like a canopy around Him. Then the LORD thunders from heaven, and out come hailstones and coals of fire.

cards.question: True or false: when the LORD shoots His arrows and hurls lightning, David's foes stand their ground.

cards.text: At the blast of the breath of His nostrils, the channels of the sea appear and the foundations of the world are exposed. Me? I sneeze and knock over a jar of sprinkles.

cards.question: After all that thunder and fire, the LORD reaches down from on high. What does He do?

answers.text: He takes hold of David and draws him out of deep waters
He tells David to climb out of the waters on his own
He sends David back into the battle by himself

cards.question: True or false: David admits his enemies were too mighty for him.

cards.text: His enemies came at him on his day of calamity, his worst day. But the LORD was his support, so he wasn't standing there alone.

cards.question: The LORD brought David out into the open and rescued him because He ___ in him.

cards.text: Now the song shifts. David says the LORD rewarded him according to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands, and friend, my hands are a MUSTACHE full of dough, so I'll just stand over here.

cards.question: David is talking about how he has lived. What does he say about the ways of the LORD?
True or false: David says he has set aside some of God's statutes.

cards.text: He says he's been blameless before Him and kept himself from iniquity. So the LORD has repaid him according to his righteousness.
Then David speaks to the LORD Himself: to the faithful You show Yourself faithful, to the blameless You show Yourself blameless, and to the pure You show Yourself pure.

cards.question: Then the pattern breaks. To the crooked, the LORD shows Himself ___.
David says the LORD saves an afflicted people. Who does the LORD humble?

cards.text: Then David says the LORD lights his lamp and lights up his darkness. Years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, so trust me, I KNOW what a little light means.

cards.question: With his God beside him, what does David say he can do?

answers.text: Charge an army and scale a wall
Outrun a chariot and cross a sea
Rule a city and build a temple

cards.text: As for God, David says, His way is perfect and the word of the LORD is flawless. I check every batch for flaws and find one EVERY time, so flawless? That's a whole other league.

cards.question: David says the LORD is a ___ to all who take refuge in Him.
David asks, "For who is God besides the LORD?" True or false: he's saying there is no God besides the LORD.

cards.text: It is God who arms David with strength and makes his way clear. He makes David's feet like those of a deer and stations him on the heights, while I'm over here hopping on a gold base and calling it CARDIO.

cards.question: The LORD trains David's hands for battle. What does David say his arms can do?
After all that battle talk, David names something surprising that exalts him. What is it?
True or false: David says the LORD narrows the path beneath him so he has to tiptoe.

cards.text: Now David tells the battle: he chases down his enemies and doesn't turn back until they're consumed. Friend, I once lost a race to a runaway chocolate chip.

cards.question: True or false: after David crushes his enemies, they get back up and come at him again.
David has been fighting hard. Who does he say armed him with strength for battle?

cards.text: His enemies retreat, and they cry for help, but there's no one to save them. They even cry out to the LORD.

cards.question: True or false: when David's enemies cry out to the LORD, He answers them.

cards.text: David says he ground them as dust in the face of the wind and trampled them like mud in the streets.
Then David says the LORD has delivered him from the strife of the people and made him the head of nations.

cards.question: The LORD has made David the head of nations. What does David say a people he had not known will do?
When foreigners hear David, they ___ him.

cards.text: Foreigners lose heart and come trembling out of their strongholds. That word again, friend: back at the start, David called the LORD HIS stronghold.
Then the praise breaks loose: "The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock!" That's not singing anymore, friend, that's SHOUTING.

cards.question: David blesses the God of his salvation, the God who avenges him. What else does David say this God does for him?
Because of all this, David says he will praise the LORD among the ___.

cards.text: And the last line: "Great salvation He brings to His king." The man Saul hunted day after day ends this song being called His king.

cards.question: The LORD shows loving devotion to His anointed. Who does it reach and for how long?

findings.problem: The joke 'I can't get two words out before my first batch' doesn't share the core action of the fact. David is piling up name after name for the LORD, but the comparison is about struggling to speak before baking. It doesn't click, and a stranger would say 'huh?'.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'his day of calamity, his worst day' stretches the text. Psalm 18:18 says 'my day of calamity' and never calls it his worst day.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The question asks who armed David with strength for battle (18:39). This repeats 18:32, 'It is God who arms me with strength', which stop 2 card 13 already told outright. Asking about the repeated line again gives the baker nothing new to reason out.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The question says 'David blesses the God of his salvation', but 18:46 says 'may the God of my salvation be exalted'. The text blesses 'my Rock', not the God of his salvation.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card calls 'Great salvation He brings to His king.' 'the last line', but 18:50 goes on with 'He shows loving devotion to His anointed…', which the next card asks about. The quoted sentence isn't the last line.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: 'The man Saul hunted day after day' states a Bible fact from 1 Samuel 23:14 without its reference. The card cites only Psalm 18:50, and the reference was given only back in stop 1 card 1.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.
